proofs.proof_tex:
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-history-envelopes}.  Its risk upper bound at \(s=0\), together with \(B_0=B(c)\leq c/3\) from \(\mathrm{lem:stable\text{-}weights}\), gives
\[
R(n,T,c)\leq\min\left\{1,\left(\frac1{2\sqrt n}+B(c)\right)^2\right\}
\leq C_R\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}
\tag{1}
\]
for a universal \(C_R\).  For the advertised interval, put \(h_n=\sqrt{\log(40)/(2n)}\).  Convexity gives \(e^{\lambda y}\leq1-y+ye^\lambda\) for \(0\leq y\leq1\).  If \(m=E_PY\), then
\[
g(\lambda)=\log(1-m+me^\lambda)-m\lambda
\tag{2}
\]
satisfies \(g(0)=g'(0)=0\) and \(g''(\lambda)\leq1/4\).  Integrating twice, using independence from \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), and applying exponential Markov inequality at \(\lambda=4h_n\) to both tails yields
\[
P^n\{|\overline Y-\mu(P)|>h_n\}\leq2e^{-2nh_n^2}=0.05.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(|\psi_T(P,c)-\mu(P)|\leq B(c)\) by \(\mathrm{lem:stable\text{-}weights}\),
\[
I_n=[\overline Y-h_n-B(c),\overline Y+h_n+B(c)]\cap[0,1]
\tag{4}
\]
is uniformly \(0.95\)-honest and connected.  Therefore
\[
L(n,T,c)\leq\min\{1,2h_n+2B(c)\}
\leq C_L\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}.
\tag{5}
\]
These are total procedures, and (4) is the natural-mean interval with a Hoeffding radius and deterministic intervention-bias radius.

Suppose now that \(T\geq2k_n\).  Then \(T>k_n\) and
\[
1-\frac{k_n}{T}\geq\frac12.
\tag{6}
\]
The two corollaries in Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-history-envelopes} and (6) imply, for universal positive \(c_R,c_L\),
\[
R(n,T,c)\geq c_R(n^{-1}+c^2),
\qquad
L(n,T,c)\geq c_L(n^{-1/2}+c).
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(n^{-1}+c^2\leq2\) and \(n^{-1/2}+c\leq2\), decreasing the constants in (7) gives the corresponding lower bounds with \(\min\{1,\cdot\}\).  Combining them with (1) and (5), and choosing common universal constants \(0<a_0\leq A_0<\infty\), proves the theorem.  All inequalities are uniform in \(n,T,c\), including \(n=1\), shrinking \(c\), deterministic treatment, and null histories.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(n,T\geq1\) and \(c\in[0,1]\), define, for \(0\leq s\leq T\),
\[
B_s=\frac12\sqrt{\exp\!\left\{\frac{c^2(T-s)}{4T}\right\}-1},
\qquad v_0=\frac1{4n},
\qquad v_s=\frac1{2n}+\frac{100c^2s4^s}{Tn}\quad(1\leq s\leq T).
\]
There are total data-dependent rules \(\widehat\psi^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\in\mathcal E_{n,T}\) and \(I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\in\mathcal C_{n,T,c}\), obtained by deterministic minimization over \(s\) and empirical prefix tries, such that
\[
R(n,T,c)\leq\min_{0\leq s\leq T}\min\{1,(\sqrt{v_s}+B_s)^2\},
\]
\[
L(n,T,c)\leq\min_{0\leq s\leq T}\min\{1,2\sqrt{20v_s}+2B_s\}.
\]
The rules require \(O(nT+T)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(nT)\) memory. Conversely, with a supremum over the empty set interpreted as zero,
\[
R(n,T,c)\geq\max\left\{\frac{3}{512n},
\sup_{1\leq k<T}\frac{b_{T-k}(\eta)^2}{8}(1-\rho_{n,k})_+\right\},
\]
\[
L(n,T,c)\geq\max\left\{\frac{0.65}{4\sqrt n},
\sup_{1\leq k<T}b_{T-k}(\eta)(0.90-\rho_{n,k})_+\right\}.
\]
Consequently, for a universal constant \(a_1>0\), whenever \(T>k_n\),
\[
R(n,T,c)\geq a_1\left\{n^{-1}+c^2\left(1-\frac{k_n}{T}\right)\right\},
\qquad
L(n,T,c)\geq a_1\left\{n^{-1/2}+c\sqrt{1-\frac{k_n}{T}}\right\}.
\]
At \(T=2\), on a leaf with positive prefix masses and with \(u=\delta-1\), the first term in the Taylor polynomial of the two denominator factors that cannot be written as a sum of separate scalar-prefix terms is
\[
u^2\frac{m_{h_1 1}(P)}{m_{h_1}(P)}
\frac{m_{h_2 1}(P)}{m_{h_2}(P)}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_T\).  We first construct the upper procedures.  For \(s\in\{0,\ldots,T\}\), let \(Q_{P,c}^{(s)}\) be the law which uses \(q_t^P\) for \(t\leq s\), uses the observational action kernel for \(t>s\), and retains all covariate and outcome kernels.  Put
\[
\psi_s(P,c)=E_{Q_{P,c}^{(s)}}[Y].
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \(\psi_0(P,c)=\mu(P)\) and \(\psi_T(P,c)\) is the target in \(\mathrm{def:estimand}\).  Under \(Q_{P,c}^{(s)}\), define the tail likelihood ratio
\[
U_s=\prod_{t=s+1}^T\frac{\delta^{A_t}}{d_t^P(H_t)},
\qquad U_T=1.
\tag{2}
\]
After time \(s\), the conditional action law under \(Q_{P,c}^{(s)}\) is the observational law under \(P\).  The conditional calculation in \(\mathrm{lem:stable\text{-}weights}\), applied successively to the \(T-s\) factors in (2), therefore gives
\[
E_{Q_{P,c}^{(s)}}[U_s]=1,
\qquad
E_{Q_{P,c}^{(s)}}[U_s^2]
 \leq\cosh(\eta/2)^{2(T-s)}
 \leq\exp\!\left\{\frac{c^2(T-s)}{4T}\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The first equality uses no division by a zero treatment probability: when a treatment is deterministic, its likelihood-ratio factor equals one on its support.  By sequential factorization, \(dQ_{P,c}/dQ_{P,c}^{(s)}=U_s\) on the latter law's support.  Since \(0\leq Y\leq1\) by \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}outcome}\), \(\operatorname{Var}_{Q_{P,c}^{(s)}}(Y)\leq1/4\).  Equations (1)--(3) and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\psi_T(P,c)-\psi_s(P,c)|
 &=\left|E_{Q_{P,c}^{(s)}}[(Y-E_{Q_{P,c}^{(s)}}Y)(U_s-1)]\right|\\
 &\leq\frac12\sqrt{E_{Q_{P,c}^{(s)}}[U_s^2]-1}
 \leq B_s.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

We next estimate \(\psi_s\).  The case \(s=0\) uses
\[
\widehat\psi_0=\overline Y=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nY_i,
\qquad
E_{P^n}[(\widehat\psi_0-\psi_0)^2]=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_P(Y)}n\leq v_0.
\tag{5}
\]
Fix \(s\geq1\), write \(Z_{i,s}=(X_{i1},A_{i1},\ldots,X_{is},A_{is})\), and form the \(2\cdot4^s\)-coordinate fractional histogram
\[
\widehat p_{z,1}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\mathbf1\{Z_{i,s}=z\},
\qquad
\widehat p_{z,0}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(1-Y_i)\mathbf1\{Z_{i,s}=z\}.
\tag{6}
\]
Let \(p_{z,1}=E_P[Y\mathbf1\{Z_s=z\}]\) and \(p_{z,0}=E_P[(1-Y)\mathbf1\{Z_s=z\}]\).  Both \(p\) and \(\widehat p\) are probability vectors.  They define binary-outcome laws on \((Z_s,B)\), with \(E[B\mid Z_s=z]=E_P[Y\mid Z_s=z]\) for \(p\), and the analogous empirical conditional mean for \(\widehat p\).  Because the identifying functional is linear in the conditional terminal-outcome mean, \(F_{s,c_s}(p)=\psi_s(P,c)\), where
\[
c_s=c\sqrt{s/T},
\qquad 0\leq c_s\leq1,
\qquad \exp(c_s/\sqrt s)=\exp(c/\sqrt T)=\delta.
\tag{7}
\]
Here \(F_{s,c_s}\) denotes the functional in \(\mathrm{def:leaf\text{-}functional}\) at horizon \(s\) and strength \(c_s\).  Define
\[
\widehat\psi_s=F_{s,c_s}(\widehat p),
\qquad
G_s(q)=F_{s,c_s}(q)-\sum_zq_{z,1}.
\tag{8}
\]
Every vector in (8) is a legal finite observed law; it may be equipped with independent structural errors to satisfy consistency and sequential exchangeability.  Thus \(\widehat\psi_s\in[0,1]\), including at null prefixes under the convention in \(\mathrm{def:leaf\text{-}functional}\).

We establish the modulus used for (8).  For positive probability vectors \(q,q'\), put
\[
h(q,q')^2=\sum_j(\sqrt{q_j}-\sqrt{q'_j})^2,
\qquad
\vartheta=\arccos\sum_j\sqrt{q_jq'_j}\in[0,\pi/2].
\tag{9}
\]
If \(r=(\sqrt{q_j})_j\), \(r'=(\sqrt{q'_j})_j\), and \(\vartheta>0\), the arc
\[
r(t)=\frac{\sin((1-t)\vartheta)}{\sin\vartheta}r
     +\frac{\sin(t\vartheta)}{\sin\vartheta}r',
\qquad q_j(t)=r_j(t)^2,
\tag{10}
\]
has positive coordinates, unit Euclidean norm, and constant Euclidean speed \(\vartheta\).  Its score is \(S_t(j)=\dot q_j(t)/q_j(t)=2\dot r_j(t)/r_j(t)\), whence
\[
\|S_t\|_{L_2(q(t))}^2
=\sum_jq_j(t)S_t(j)^2
=4\sum_j\dot r_j(t)^2
=4\vartheta^2.
\tag{11}
\]
By \(\mathrm{prop:centered\text{-}local\text{-}bound}\), applied at horizon \(s\) and strength \(c_s\), the canonical gradient of \(G_s\) has norm at most \(2c_s\).  The defining score identity for that gradient, (10)--(11), and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
\begin{aligned}
|G_s(q')-G_s(q)|
&\leq\int_0^1\|D_{G,q(t),c_s}\|_{L_2(q(t))}\|S_t\|_{L_2(q(t))}\,dt\\
&\leq4c_s\vartheta
\leq5c_s h(q,q').
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
The last inequality follows from \(h(q,q')=2\sin(\vartheta/2)\) and \(\vartheta/h(q,q')\leq\pi/(2\sqrt2)<5/4\) on \([0,\pi/2]\).  If either endpoint lies on the boundary, replace both endpoints by \((1-\epsilon)q+\epsilon\mathbf1/K_s\), where \(K_s=2\cdot4^s\), apply (12), and let \(\epsilon\downarrow0\).  This passage is valid directly from \(\mathrm{def:leaf\text{-}functional}\): if a limiting leaf has positive mass, all its ancestor masses are positive and every displayed ratio is continuous; if its mass is zero, its outcome-weighted contribution is bounded by \(\delta^s\) times that leaf mass and tends to zero.  Hence (12) holds on the closed simplex and never divides by a null prefix.

For each coordinate with \(p_j>0\),
\[
(\sqrt{\widehat p_j}-\sqrt{p_j})^2
=\frac{(\widehat p_j-p_j)^2}{(\sqrt{\widehat p_j}+\sqrt{p_j})^2}
\leq\frac{(\widehat p_j-p_j)^2}{p_j}.
\tag{13}
\]
The summand defining \(\widehat p_j\) lies in \([0,1]\), has mean \(p_j\), and the observations are independent by \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), so \(\operatorname{Var}(\widehat p_j)\leq p_j/n\).  If \(p_j=0\), then \(\widehat p_j=0\) almost surely.  Summing (13) over the \(K_s=2\cdot4^s\) coordinates yields
\[
E_{P^n}[h(\widehat p,p)^2]\leq\frac{2\cdot4^s}{n}.
\tag{14}
\]
Since \(\sum_z\widehat p_{z,1}=\overline Y\), equations (8), (12), and (14), followed by \((x+y)^2\leq2x^2+2y^2\), give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{P^n}[(\widehat\psi_s-\psi_s)^2]
&\leq2E_{P^n}[(\overline Y-E_PY)^2]
  +2E_{P^n}[(G_s(\widehat p)-G_s(p))^2]\\
&\leq\frac1{2n}+50c_s^2\frac{2\cdot4^s}{n}
=\frac1{2n}+\frac{100c^2s4^s}{Tn}=v_s.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
\]
Combining (4) and (15) with the triangle inequality in \(L_2(P^n)\) gives
\[
E_{P^n}[(\widehat\psi_s-\psi_T(P,c))^2]
\leq(\sqrt{v_s}+B_s)^2.
\tag{16}
\]
Both \(\widehat\psi_s\) and the target lie in \([0,1]\), so the left side is also at most one.

Let \(s_R\) be the least minimizer of \(\min\{1,(\sqrt{v_s}+B_s)^2\}\), and set \(\widehat\psi^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}=\widehat\psi_{s_R}\).  This is one data-driven estimator, selected using only \((n,T,c)\), so (16) and \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\) prove the displayed risk upper bound.  Let \(s_L\) be the least minimizer of \(\min\{1,2\sqrt{20v_s}+2B_s\}\) and define
\[
I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}
=\left[\widehat\psi_{s_L}-\sqrt{20v_{s_L}}-B_{s_L},
        \widehat\psi_{s_L}+\sqrt{20v_{s_L}}+B_{s_L}\right]\cap[0,1].
\tag{17}
\]
By (15) and Markov's inequality,
\[
P^n\{|\widehat\psi_{s_L}-\psi_{s_L}|>\sqrt{20v_{s_L}}\}\leq\frac1{20}.
\tag{18}
\]
Equations (4), (17), and (18) give coverage at least \(0.95\), uniformly in \(P\).  The intersection in (17) is connected, and its length is bounded by \(\min\{1,2\sqrt{20v_{s_L}}+2B_{s_L}\}\).  Hence \(I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\in\mathcal C_{n,T,c}\), and \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}length}\) proves the length upper bound.

For explicit computation, first evaluate the \(T+1\) pairs \((B_s,v_s)\) and the two least minimizers, capping an objective at one as soon as it exceeds one.  For a selected positive depth, insert each observed prefix into a binary trie.  At every visited history store its count and treated-child count, giving
\[
\widehat\pi_t(h)=\frac{\sum_i\mathbf1\{H_{it}=h,A_{it}=1\}}
{\sum_i\mathbf1\{H_{it}=h\}}.
\tag{19}
\]
Only histories visited by an observation are evaluated, so every denominator in (19) is positive.  A second pass computes each observed product \(\prod_{t\leq s}\delta^{A_{it}}/\{1+(\delta-1)\widehat\pi_t(H_{it})\}\) and its \(Y_i\)-weighted average, which equals (8) by grouping observations by terminal prefix.  There are at most \(ns\) visited trie nodes.  Computing both selected depths, without attempting to share their tries, therefore uses \(O(nT+T)\) arithmetic and \(O(nT)\) memory.  The case \(s=0\) uses (5), so the algorithm is total for all \(n,T,c\), including deterministic actions and null histories.

For the mixed-prefix audit, take \(T=2\), put \(u=\delta-1\), and, on a fixed leaf with positive prefix masses, set
\[
p_j=\frac{m_{h_j1}(P)}{m_{h_j}(P)},\qquad j=1,2.
\tag{20}
\]
Multiplying the degree-two Taylor polynomials at \(u=0\) gives
\[
\frac1{(1+up_1)(1+up_2)}
=1-u(p_1+p_2)+u^2(p_1^2+p_2^2+p_1p_2)+O(u^3).
\tag{21}
\]
The terms through degree one and the two square terms are sums of functions of one prefix ratio; the cross term \(u^2p_1p_2\) is the first term involving both an ancestor prefix and its descendant.  It is not additively scalar: its rectangular cross-difference at \((p_1,p_2),(p'_1,p_2),(p_1,p'_2),(p'_1,p'_2)\) is \(u^2(p_1-p'_1)(p_2-p'_2)\), whereas the cross-difference of \(f(p_1)+g(p_2)\) is zero.  The numerator \(\delta^{a_1+a_2}\) is independent of the prefix masses and does not remove this distinction.  If an ancestor prefix is null, every descendant leaf has zero mass and hence zero outcome-weighted contribution in \(\mathrm{def:leaf\text{-}functional}\); thus the audit makes no division at a null prefix.

We now prove the converses.  First take two laws \(P_-\) and \(P_+\) for which all covariates and actions are deterministically zero and every potential terminal outcome equals a common Bernoulli random variable of mean
\[
\theta_-=\frac12-d,
\qquad \theta_+=\frac12+d,
\qquad d=\frac1{8\sqrt n}.
\tag{22}
\]
Consistency and sequential exchangeability hold because the common potential outcome is independent of the deterministic actions, so both laws belong to \(\mathcal P_T\) by \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).  The intervention leaves the deterministic action law unchanged; hence \(\psi_T(P_\pm,c)=\theta_\pm\).  The one-observation Hellinger affinity of the outcome laws is \(\sqrt{1-4d^2}\), and product factorization gives affinity \((1-4d^2)^{n/2}\).  For any two probability mass functions \(f,g\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\operatorname{TV}(f,g)
=\frac12\sum_x|\sqrt{f(x)}-\sqrt{g(x)}|\{\sqrt{f(x)}+\sqrt{g(x)}\}
\leq\sqrt{1-\left(\sum_x\sqrt{f(x)g(x)}\right)^2}.
\tag{23}
\]
For completeness, \((1-x)^m\geq1-mx\) for \(x\in[0,1]\) follows by induction: multiplication of the induction hypothesis by \(1-x\geq0\) gives \((1-x)^{m+1}\geq1-(m+1)x+mx^2\geq1-(m+1)x\).  Taking \(m=n\) and \(x=1/(16n)\) gives \((1-1/(16n))^n\geq15/16\).  Thus (22)--(23) give
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_-^n,P_+^n)\leq\frac14.
\tag{24}
\]
Given any estimator, test \(P_+\) exactly when the estimate is at least \(1/2\).  On either testing-error event its squared error under the corresponding law is at least \(d^2\).  If its worst-case risk is \(\mathcal R\), the sum of the two testing-error probabilities is at most \(2\mathcal R/d^2\).  On the other hand, for every test with acceptance event \(A\),
\[
P_-^n(A)+P_+^n(A^c)
=1-\{P_+^n(A)-P_-^n(A)\}
\geq1-\operatorname{TV}(P_-^n,P_+^n)\geq\frac34.
\tag{25}
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal R\geq3d^2/8=3/(512n)\), and taking the infimum proves the first risk floor.

For an honest connected interval \(I\), honesty under \(P_-\) and (24) imply
\[
P_+^n\{\theta_-\in I\}\geq0.95-0.25=0.70.
\tag{26}
\]
Honesty under \(P_+\) gives \(P_+^n\{\theta_+\in I\}\geq0.95\).  The union bound makes the probability of their intersection at least \(0.65\).  Connectedness then forces length at least \(\theta_+-\theta_-=2d=1/(4\sqrt n)\), so
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_T}E_{P^n}[\operatorname{length}(I)]\geq\frac{0.65}{4\sqrt n}.
\tag{27}
\]
The argument includes independent randomization by taking product with the same randomization law, which leaves total variation unchanged.

Finally fix \(1\leq k<T\), put \(r_0=T-k\), and abbreviate \(b=b_{r_0}(\eta)\) and \(\rho=\rho_{n,k}\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:paired\text{-}witness\text{-}audit}\), the simple experiment \((P_0^{k,r_0})^n\) has target \(\theta_1=1/2+b\), every fixed law in \(\overline P_1^{(n,k,r_0)}\) has target \(\theta_0=1/2\), and the total variation between the simple experiment and the mixture is at most \(\rho\).  If \(b=0\), both desired paired lower bounds have zero right side and are immediate.  Suppose \(b>0\).  Testing according to which target is nearer to an arbitrary estimator incurs squared error at least \(b^2/4\) on either error event.  If \(\mathcal R\) is the estimator's worst-case risk, its error sum is at most \(8\mathcal R/b^2\), whereas the identity in (25) bounds that sum below by \((1-\rho)_+\).  Therefore
\[
\mathcal R\geq\frac{b^2}{8}(1-\rho)_+.
\tag{28}
\]
For an honest interval, averaging coverage of \(\theta_0\) over the fixed alternatives and transferring it to the simple experiment loses at most \(\rho\).  Intersecting that event with the \(0.95\)-coverage event for \(\theta_1\) gives probability at least \((0.90-\rho)_+\) that both endpoints lie in the interval.  Hence
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_T}E_{P^n}[\operatorname{length}(I)]
\geq b(0.90-\rho)_+.
\tag{29}
\]
Equations (25)--(29), followed by the two infima in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\) and \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}length}\), prove both every-\(k\) displays.

If \(T>k_n\), choose \(k=k_n\).  By the definition of \(k_n\),
\[
\rho_{n,k_n}\leq\frac{n(n-1)}{4^{k_n}}\leq0.01,
\qquad
b_{T-k_n}(\eta)\geq\frac c{16}\sqrt{1-\frac{k_n}{T}},
\tag{30}
\]
where the second inequality is part of \(\mathrm{lem:paired\text{-}witness\text{-}audit}\).  Substitution in (28)--(29) and combination with (25) and (27), using \(\max\{x,y\}\geq(x+y)/2\), gives the two final corollaries for a sufficiently small universal \(a_1>0\).
added_lemmas.justification: The proposition gives total finite-data upper procedures and unrestricted every-depth testing converses on the same model class.
added_lemmas.gap: Its optimized upper and lower envelopes are not claimed to coincide in the intermediate factor-two logarithmic elbow.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is the computable bracket and the sole substantive input to the clean long-history corollary.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
In the only regime not matched by \(\mathrm{prop:finite\text{-}history\text{-}envelopes}\), namely the factor-two logarithmic elbow between full-prefix plug-in control near \(4^T\leq n\) and collision-converse activation near \(4^k\geq100n^2\), use the proposed program \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{tree}}\) to determine the optimal compatible-tree approximation and testing scale for \(G_{T,c}(P)\).  The approximation must give explicit polynomial degrees and coefficients, an explicit multinomial factorial or degenerate \(U\)-statistic retaining nested-count covariance, and dual priors supported on legal subtrees.  It must handle null prefixes and saturation and account for the first non-scalar two-prefix term
\[
(\delta-1)^2\frac{m_{h_1 1}(P)}{m_{h_1}(P)}
\frac{m_{h_2 1}(P)}{m_{h_2}(P)},
\]
whose descendant denominator is constrained by the ancestor parent-sum identity.  Determine whether the approximation, variance, and fixed-sample testing scales coincide throughout this elbow.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The finite-history envelopes, null-prefix treatment, and first mixed-prefix term are now proved in Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-history-envelopes}; the genuinely unresolved content is only the joint approximation, nested-variance, and legal-prior theorem across the factor-two logarithmic elbow.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Close the remaining factor-two logarithmic elbow isolated in \(\mathrm{oeq:compatible\text{-}prefix\text{-}approximation}\).  Refine the computable truncated-prefix upper functions and every-depth paired lower functions in \(\mathrm{prop:finite\text{-}history\text{-}envelopes}\) into matching evaluable functions \(r(n,T,c)\) and \(\ell(n,T,c)\) on that elbow, with a total finite-data estimator and a calibrated honest connected interval.  Splice the result with \(\mathrm{prop:endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) and \(\mathrm{thm:long\text{-}history\text{-}frontier}\) to obtain the all-sample transition, including saturation and shrinking \(c\), and then give necessary and sufficient consistency and oracle-order-penalty conditions along arbitrary sequences \((T_n,c_n)\).  State finite computational cost, and keep both converses on the original fixed-\(n\) iid experiment over the same class \(\mathcal P_T\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The zero-shift endpoint, an all-domain computable bracket, and the long-history matched phase are established, so the remaining question is the matched interpolation on the unresolved elbow and its all-sequence consequences.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: The handle \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{tree}}\) denotes the following proposed, not yet certified approximation program for \(G_{T,c}(P)\): partition unconditional subtree-root masses into dyadic occupancy ranges; approximate rational descendant contributions jointly in unconditional child masses subject to every parent-sum identity; lift the resulting mixed monomials by multinomial factorial moments or degenerate \(U\)-statistics while retaining covariance between nested prefixes; and seek dual moment-matched priors whose draws are whole legal subtrees.  No polynomial degree, coefficient array, variance certificate, or legal prior pair is asserted by this definition.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The current imperative wording can be read as though the approximation, statistic, variance certificate, and legal priors were constructed.  The corrected construction names only a proposed research program and expressly withholds those unproved objects.

proposed.statement:
In the only regime not matched by \(\mathrm{prop:finite\text{-}history\text{-}envelopes}\), namely the factor-two logarithmic elbow between full-prefix plug-in control near \(4^T\leq n\) and collision-converse activation near \(4^k\geq100n^2\), use the proposed program \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{tree}}\) to determine the optimal compatible-tree approximation and testing scale for \(G_{T,c}(P)\).  The approximation must give explicit polynomial degrees and coefficients, an explicit multinomial factorial or degenerate \(U\)-statistic retaining nested-count covariance, and dual priors supported on legal subtrees.  It must handle null prefixes and saturation and account for the first non-scalar two-prefix term
\[
(\delta-1)^2\frac{m_{h_1 1}(P)}{m_{h_1}(P)}
\frac{m_{h_2 1}(P)}{m_{h_2}(P)},
\]
whose descendant denominator is constrained by the ancestor parent-sum identity.  Determine whether the approximation, variance, and fixed-sample testing scales coincide throughout this elbow.

proposed.statement: Close the remaining factor-two logarithmic elbow isolated in \(\mathrm{oeq:compatible\text{-}prefix\text{-}approximation}\).  Refine the computable truncated-prefix upper functions and every-depth paired lower functions in \(\mathrm{prop:finite\text{-}history\text{-}envelopes}\) into matching evaluable functions \(r(n,T,c)\) and \(\ell(n,T,c)\) on that elbow, with a total finite-data estimator and a calibrated honest connected interval.  Splice the result with \(\mathrm{prop:endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) and \(\mathrm{thm:long\text{-}history\text{-}frontier}\) to obtain the all-sample transition, including saturation and shrinking \(c\), and then give necessary and sufficient consistency and oracle-order-penalty conditions along arbitrary sequences \((T_n,c_n)\).  State finite computational cost, and keep both converses on the original fixed-\(n\) iid experiment over the same class \(\mathcal P_T\).

proposed.statement: There exist universal constants \(0<a_0\leq A_0<\infty\) such that, whenever \(T\geq2k_n\), \(a_0\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\leq R(n,T,c)\leq A_0\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\) and \(a_0\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\leq L(n,T,c)\leq A_0\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\). The upper estimator is the clipped natural sample mean, the interval adds the deterministic radius \(B(c)\) to a Hoeffding radius, and the lower bounds range over every measurable estimator and every possibly randomized honest connected interval.

proposed.comparator_claim: The general identification model contains the present binary complete-case subclass after retention is fixed to one, but Theorem 6.1 instead assumes a common constant positive propensity; deterministic late propensities place the paired alternatives outside that special class, so only the present converse transfers upward to the general model and no result transfers to the Theorem 6.1 class.
The paper derives and attains local efficiency bounds for behavior-dependent tilting and modified-treatment policies under Markov or non-Markov policy models.
The paper develops one-stage switching, low-count polynomial, and behavior-mixture machinery for a fixed target policy, without nested longitudinal arms.
The paper proves discrete one-time causal minimax bounds driven by unseen contexts and within-cell collisions, without sequential parent-sum compatibility.
The paper characterizes a parametric fixed-policy history-length bias--variance tradeoff rather than an unrestricted minimax frontier.
CoinDICE constructs behavior-agnostic policy-value intervals from embedded Markov occupancy equations and proves asymptotic and nonasymptotic coverage statements.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A common sharp scale for compatible-tree rational approximation, the second moment of its explicit multinomial factorial statistic, and fixed-sample dual priors supported on legal subtrees throughout the factor-two logarithmic elbow.
open_obligations.obstruction: Ancestor and descendant prefix masses recur in the same denominator product and obey parent-sum identities.  Independent scalar moment lifts miss the first mixed term, while a uniform polynomial error alone controls neither nested-count covariance nor the affinity of legal fixed-sample subtree mixtures.
open_obligations.attempted: Expanded the two-prefix product, proved the centered Hellinger modulus through boundary laws, built and optimized every truncated empirical prefix plug-in, and combined these upper bounds with every-depth complementary-context mixtures.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-history-envelopes} proves the all-domain truncated-prefix upper functions
\[
\min_{0\leq s\leq T}\min\{1,(\sqrt{v_s}+B_s)^2\},
\qquad
\min_{0\leq s\leq T}\min\{1,2\sqrt{20v_s}+2B_s\},
\]
and the every-depth lower functions
\[
\max_{1\leq k<T}\frac{b_{T-k}(\eta)^2}{8}(1-\rho_{n,k})_+,
\qquad
\max_{1\leq k<T}b_{T-k}(\eta)(0.90-\rho_{n,k})_+,
\]
in addition to the explicit parametric floors.  At two positive-mass prefixes, expansion of
\[
\prod_{t=1}^2\frac1{1+(\delta-1)m_{h_t1}(P)/m_{h_t}(P)}
\]
through second order shows that the first term not reducible to separate scalar approximations is
\[
(\delta-1)^2\frac{m_{h_1 1}(P)}{m_{h_1}(P)}
\frac{m_{h_2 1}(P)}{m_{h_2}(P)}.
\]
The descendant mass in the second ratio is constrained by the first prefix's parent-sum identity.  Null-prefix descendant leaf contributions vanish, so this algebra introduces no division at a null prefix.  These results isolate, but do not close, the factor-two logarithmic elbow.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Matching evaluable risk and honest-length functions on the intermediate factor-two logarithmic elbow, and therefore necessary and sufficient consistency and oracle-penalty conditions for arbitrary sequences.
open_obligations.obstruction: The theorem depends on the unresolved compatible-prefix approximation and testing dual.  The proved upper and lower finite optimizations match at zero shift and beyond the birthday-collision depth but need not coincide between those endpoints.
open_obligations.attempted: Combined empirical truncated trees, the dimension-free centered gradient, natural-mean bias control, Bernoulli floors, and complementary-context mixtures over every admissible depth; the resulting bracket is explicit but not sharp in the elbow.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved finite-sample bracket is Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-history-envelopes}.  At \(c=0\), \(\mathrm{prop:endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) gives \(R(n,T,0)\asymp n^{-1}\) and \(L(n,T,0)\asymp n^{-1/2}\) for every \(T\).  If \(T\geq2k_n\), \(\mathrm{thm:long\text{-}history\text{-}frontier}\) gives
\[
R(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\},
\qquad
L(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}.
\]
In that long-history regime and along \(n\to\infty\), consistency is equivalent to \(c_n\to0\).  Using \(\mathrm{prop:oracle\text{-}benchmark}\), unknown and oracle orders agree exactly when \(c_n=O(n^{-1/2})\); their risk and length ratios have orders \(1+nc_n^2\) and \(1+\sqrt n c_n\), respectively.  The remaining intermediate-depth bounds are explicit and computable but not known to match.

prose_updates.tldr: The unknown-propensity problem has a proved, computable finite-history bracket and a matched long-history phase.  A truncated empirical prefix-trie estimator and a Markov-calibrated connected interval give explicit upper envelopes optimized over prefix depth, while complementary-context mixtures give explicit every-depth lower envelopes.  Once \(T\geq2\lceil\log_4(100n^2)\rceil\), these bounds match at \(R(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\) and \(L(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\); at \(c=0\) the rates are \(n^{-1}\) and \(n^{-1/2}\) for every \(T\).  The exact factor-two logarithmic elbow between full-prefix estimation near \(4^T\leq n\) and birthday-collision activation near \(4^k\geq100n^2\) remains open.

project_justification.gap: Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi derive identification, efficient influence functions, and nuisance-controlled fixed-horizon inference, but their growing-horizon theorem is a variance comparison under a common constant positive propensity.  Existing one-stage large-alphabet polynomial estimators and moment-matching converses do not enforce the parent-sum identities or nested-count covariance of a longitudinal history tree.  No inspected result closes the factor-two logarithmic elbow left between the proved truncated-tree upper envelope and the proved collision converse.
project_justification.niche: The centered finite-tree functional has a dimension-free local gradient, yet unrestricted unknown histories create a global sparse-context penalty.  The proved finite-depth bracket makes both sides computable on the original iid trajectory experiment and isolates the remaining issue: joint approximation of ancestor--descendant propensity ratios with a variance-matched factorial statistic and legal-subtree testing priors.
project_justification.fill: This note proves exact finite-tree identification, stable likelihood-ratio and local-gradient bounds, explicit finite-history upper and lower envelopes, total \(O(nT+T)\)-time prefix-trie procedures, the zero-shift endpoint, and the matched birthday-depth phase.  Constructing the unresolved polynomial or factorial correction with explicit degrees and coefficients, proving its nested-count second-moment bound, calibrating the corresponding sharper interval, constructing a matching legal-subtree converse, and evaluating the full intermediate optimization are future work rather than accomplished results.

prose_updates.related_work: Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi, \cite{KimKennedyNaimi2021}, Introduction, Theorems 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, and 6.1, and the concluding discussion, identify longitudinal incremental effects and develop fixed-horizon efficiency and nuisance-rate inference; their Theorem 6.1 instead compares variances under a common constant positive propensity.  The binary complete-case bounded-terminal-outcome class used here embeds as a subclass of their general identification model by taking every retention indicator to be one and filling unused intermediate outcomes, but it is neither their full published class nor their Theorem 6.1 class.  In particular, the paired alternatives here have deterministic late propensities.  Therefore a lower converse proved here transfers upward to their general model, an upper bound here remains restricted to the present binary complete-case class, and no result here transfers to their special Theorem 6.1 class.  Kennedy, \cite{Kennedy2019JASA}, supplies the support-respecting binary incremental functional and fixed-horizon efficiency theory.  Kallus and Uehara, \cite{KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies}, derive local efficiency theory for behavior-dependent policies under additional policy-model structure.  Ma, Zhu, Jiao, and Wainwright, \cite{MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022}, and Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015}, provide one-stage low-count polynomial and factorial-moment methods, while Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete}, analyze one-time discrete causal functionals.  None of those results supplies a joint approximation, covariance, and testing theorem for compatible nested prefixes.  Static-tilt results in \cite{SchindlShenKennedy2024} and \cite{HuangDongLinAntonelli2026} do not apply because Proposition~\ref{prop:static-nonreduction} rules out a single-normalizer reduction.  History-conditioned importance-sampling comparisons in \cite{ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025} and \cite{LiuBaconBrunskill2020}, and Markov occupancy intervals in \cite{DaiEtAl2020CoinDICE}, impose structures absent from \(\mathcal P_T\).  Higher-order influence-function machinery in \cite{RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2016TR} motivates factorial corrections but does not supply the missing tree-specific certificate.
prose_updates.interpretation:
\section{Results at a glance}
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-history-envelopes} supplies explicit upper and lower functions for every \(n,T,c\), a total empirical prefix-trie estimator, and an honest connected interval.  Theorem~\ref{thm:long-history-frontier} shows that the functions match beyond the birthday-collision depth, despite uniformly bounded oracle weights and local efficient-influence-function norm.  Proposition~\ref{prop:endpoint-reduction} gives the ordinary bounded-mean rates at zero shift, and Proposition~\ref{prop:oracle-benchmark} gives the uniform oracle rates.  The two open questions now concern only the intermediate factor-two logarithmic elbow and its all-sequence consequences.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-history envelopes are rigorous but need not match in the intermediate region between full-prefix plug-in control near \(4^T\leq n\) and collision-converse activation near \(4^k\geq100n^2\).  Closing that factor-two logarithmic elbow requires explicit joint polynomial coefficients, a multinomial nested-count second-moment theorem, and dual priors supported on legal subtrees.  A scalar approximation or independent-Poisson prefix calculation cannot certify those requirements.  Thus no complete all-sequence consistency or oracle-penalty characterization is claimed outside the zero-shift and matched long-history regimes.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Identification is given.  The statistical model is the unrestricted binary, completely observed, bounded-terminal-outcome class, with no overlap floor, Markov property, smoothness, sparsity, or supplied nuisance kernel.  The finite-history bracket, total algorithms, long-history matched theorem, zero-shift reduction, oracle benchmark, and local-gradient bound are proved on this class, including deterministic actions and null histories.  This class embeds in the general Kim--Kennedy--Naimi identification model after retention is fixed to one, so its lower converses transfer upward, but its upper bounds do not establish results for that full model.  The deterministic late propensities also place the paired alternatives outside their Theorem 6.1 common-positive-propensity class, to which no result here is transferred.  The theory is not a numerical sample-size prescription for the richer EAGeR dropout analysis.
